note: Per-slide audio-briefing speaker notes for the ESFCU CEO board briefing (Presentation Mode). Highlights only — spoken like a live meeting, not a read-out of the slide. Numbers are spelled for natural text-to-speech. Keyed by slide id (mirrors SLIDE_IDS in presentationChat.js). Slide 1 opens with the greeting.

narration.situational: Good morning, Girado. Here's your board briefing. The position is strong — roughly one-point-three-six billion in assets, about eighty-four thousand members, and a net worth ratio of nine-point-six-two percent, well capitalized. One thing needs managing: loan demand is outpacing member deposit growth, and loan-to-share is near eighty-nine percent and rising.
narration.evidence: Here's the ground under that number. Net loans of one-point-oh-four billion, up six-point-four percent year over year, against total shares of one-point-one-six billion, up just three-point-one. That gap is what lifted loan-to-share to eighty-nine-point-seven, and it's thinning on-hand liquidity to around eleven-point-two percent. Three sources, one governed figure, ninety-four percent confidence.
narration.trajectory: And here's the shape of it over eight quarters. The two balance lines separate steadily — loans climbing faster than shares — carrying the ratio from eighty-four-point-four to eighty-nine-point-seven. On the current trend it approaches the internal policy ceiling by the first quarter. The trend, not the level, is the story.
narration.members: It's worth remembering whose money this is. Educational Systems has served Maryland's education community since nineteen fifty-five — teachers, staff, and their families — across thirteen branches, and since November twenty twenty-four the Howard University division as well. That mission is why the funding question matters, and the recognition speaks for itself: the A-A-C-U-C Hall of Fame, and the Washington Business Journal's twenty twenty-five Diversity in Business Award.
narration.assurance: Before the recommendation, a word on trust. Six of seven sources loaded and reconciled by six-oh-two this morning. The seventh — the Howard University division nightly job — stalled, so that reconciliation is pending and the consolidated deposit figure is held back. It's flagged, not hidden. Every other figure traces to source, board and examiner ready.
narration.resolution: So, three paths. A deposit campaign alone is fast and cheap but only moderate in impact. A standby funding line alone buys certainty but doesn't move the trend. My recommendation is the third: pair them. The campaign moves the trend while the line holds the buffer through the first quarter if uptake lands at the low edge of the seasonality band.
narration.nextSteps: And here's what I'm asking. One — launch the education-community deposit campaign within six weeks, timed to the fall inflow window. Two — bring the standby funding line to the board next meeting. Three — close the Howard University division reconciliation before the next pre-read. Clear actions, named owners, and a timeframe on each. Thank you.
